allocate

/AL-uh-kayt/ - rhymes with gate · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Allocate means to distribute or set aside for a particular purpose.

Before the voyage, the captain allocated the hold: a third for water, a third for cargo, the rest for spare canvas.

Example

Ninety garden beds, one hundred forty applicants. The committee spent a full evening allocating them: two beds to each family with children, one to each single household, four kept back for the school's science classes. By nine o'clock every bed had a name attached, and every applicant knew exactly where they stood.

Allocate is the exact word for what the committee did, because allocate means to distribute or set aside for a particular purpose — every share came with a label. Divide would only tell us the beds were split; allocate tells us each portion was matched to a use and a recipient on purpose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

apportion: Apportion means to divide something by rule into fair shares — the courtroom and census word, where the formula matters most. Allocate is broader and more practical: a committee can allocate by any reasoning it likes, so long as each portion of the whole ends up matched to a purpose and a recipient.

assign: Assign matches one item, seat, or duty to one recipient — no dividing needed, no larger pool implied. Allocate works on a whole: to allocate is to split a limited pool and hand each portion to a purpose. You assign a locker; you allocate the school's whole bank of them.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

pool: throw every share back into one undivided pot

hold back: keep it unassigned, promised to nothing

Where it sits · how firmly each share is committed

divide → allocate → earmark

divide vs. allocate: Divide is looser than allocate — the pie is merely sliced into portions, with no slice yet promised to anyone or anything; an allocated slice carries a purpose before the meeting ends.

earmark vs. allocate: Earmark goes further than allocate — an allocated share can be reshuffled at the next meeting; an earmarked one is welded to its purpose.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — al-: to, toward (Latin ad-, assimilated)

Root — loc: place (Latin locus)

Suffix — -ate: to make, to act

Put it together: Al- (toward) + loc (place) + -ate = to set toward a place. Latin locus is a place or position; allocating money literally gives each share its own assigned spot — this much filed here, that much filed there.

Use the root in a new word: dislocate: One bad fall on the ice was enough to dislocate her shoulder and end the tournament early.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / administrative

Allocate is budget-table language — committees, treasurers, quartermasters. Its mirror in this unit is aggregate: aggregating gathers parts into one total, allocating deals one total out into labeled parts. Earmark goes narrower and firmer, welding a single share to a single purpose; in casual talk, set aside says it plainly.
